options.summary: Show the command usage
options.detail: --help prints the same usage after this subcommand. --help-all requests the full option list. Both Ubuntu packages print the same text for all three spellings.

options.summary: Detach HEAD in the new worktree
options.detail: Alias of --detach. Supply the path and optionally a commit. Without a commit the new worktree starts at HEAD.

options.summary: Create an empty worktree on an unborn branch
options.detail: Use the path basename for the branch or supply -b NAME. Omit the start commit, --detach, --track and --no-checkout. --no-orphan cancels an explicit orphan request.

options.summary: Set the starting branch as the new branch’s upstream
options.detail: Use when creating a branch, for example --track -b TOPIC PATH MAIN. This switch takes no value. Worktree add rejects --track=direct and --track=inherit.

options.summary: Create the branch without setting an upstream
options.detail: Use when a new branch would otherwise track its start point. A separate value is a positional operand.

options.summary: Base a path-named branch on a matching remote-tracking branch
options.detail: With no explicit start point, use a unique match for the path basename as the upstream. With no match, start at HEAD. For unresolved multiple matches, Git 2.43 and 2.53 fall back to HEAD while upstream 2.56 fails. checkout.defaultRemote can resolve a tie.

options.summary: Disable remote guessing for a path-named branch
options.detail: Overrides worktree.guessRemote. With no explicit start point, use the local branch matching the basename or create it at HEAD.

options.summary: Write relative links between the repository and worktree
options.detail: Overrides worktree.useRelativePaths. Enables the repository extension extensions.relativeWorktrees, which older clients cannot read. Git 2.53 and upstream support this option. Ubuntu 24.04 rejects it.

options.summary: Write absolute links for the new worktree
options.detail: Absolute paths are the default. Overrides worktree.useRelativePaths without disabling an existing repository extension. Git 2.53 and upstream support this option. Ubuntu 24.04 rejects it.

description: Create a linked working tree at the specified path.
